subject: Hemisync integration: SDK/auth, regional failover & routing policy
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Cheng <sophia@hemisync.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T17:15:00Z
Subject: Hemisync demo — follow-ups & infra questions

Hi Sophia,

Thanks again for the time today — demo looked great and the team had some good clarifying questions that I'll summarize below so we can land the integration plan. High-level asks from your side were: low-latency inference for conversational search, embeddings for semantic search + reranking, and a fallover path to a lower-cost model during peak usage.

Notes / open questions for engineering:
- SDK & auth: you mentioned a dev account today. Do you prefer API keys (fastest) or mutual TLS (required for private VPC/on-prem)? If mTLS, we'll schedule a short handoff with infra.
- Region routing: primary in us-west, but failover to us-east required. Are there regulatory constraints that force data to stay in us-west for some query types?
- Latency SLOs: target 95th < 250ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens). We'll propose batching and a KV prefix cache for chat sessions.
- Cost policy: do you want a latency-first policy (cost be damned) or a cost cap that will route to a cheaper quantized variant under burst? Example policy we can implement: prefer Llama-70B (baseline) until 95th latency > 250ms, then route to 13B-quantized fallback.
- Structured output / tool-calling: you mentioned webhook-led actions (order lookup). Do you want Redwood to call back your tool endpoints, or to return structured JSON for your runner to call?
- Embeddings / reranker: you said 1M document index; we'll recommend batched embedding ingestion + an on-demand reranker that runs top-10 candidates through a reranker model (smaller, cheaper).

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev spike: our engineers (Dev + Laura) will produce a short SDK quickstart and an auth options doc by 2028-03-15.
2) Mutual Action Plan: I'll drop a draft MAP in Drive and HubSpot (link below) with milestones and owners.
3) Technical handoff call: 30 minutes with your platform engineer (Ethan?) to confirm mTLS cert exchange or API key flow.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (recording), sample SLA sketch (inline).

If that aligns, I'll push the MAP and the quickstart later this week.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Cheng <sophia@hemisync.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-13T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Hemisync demo — follow-ups & infra questions

Thanks Mateo — quick engineering notes from our side. I pulled together the minimal configuration paths we recommend depending on your deployment mode.

If you go hosted (Redwood API):
- Auth: API key scoped down per-environment. Quick to get started.
- Region routing: route-prefix (us-west) + failover policy to us-east. Example routing rule: {match: locality==us-west, prefer: model-v1, fallback: model-v1-quantized, max_p95_latency_ms:250}.

If you go Private (VPC / mTLS):
- Auth: mTLS (recommended for production). We'll provide cert signing steps and a small ansible script to rotate certs monthly.
- Network: allowlist Redwood egress IPs or set up a peering connection.

Model routing & policy configuration (concrete):
- Policy primitives: prefer_model (string), max_p95_latency_ms (int), cost_threshold_usd_per_1k_tokens (float), region_preference (list).
- Example fallback chain: [llama-70b, redwood-13b-8bit, redwood-7b-8bit] with explicit latency and cost thresholds.
- KV caching: configure per-conversation TTL of 3600s for short-term context reuse.

Structured output / tool calling:
- Option A (Redwood calls your webhook): Redwood will POST structured JSON + HMAC signature to your tool endpoint; you return 200 + verb to execute.
- Option B (return structured JSON): Redwood returns a typed JSON payload that your runtime will use to execute. This is slightly lower trust surface and easier to audit.

Embeddings / reranker pattern:
1) Batch embed documents with batching size ~512 and quantize vectors for storage.
2) Use approximate nearest neighbors to fetch top-100, then run reranker (small encoder-decoder ~1-3B) to produce final top-10.

Quick config sample (SDK):
```yaml
redwood:
  api_key: <REDACTED>
  region: us-west
  routing:
    prefer_model: llama-70b
    fallback_chain: [redwood-13b-8bit, redwood-7b-8bit]
    p95_threshold_ms: 250
```

I'll attach a one-page SDK quickstart and a short checklist for mTLS and vault integration. Happy to join the handoff call — suggested times below.

— Dev
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sdk_quickstart.yml]
From: Sophia Cheng <sophia@hemisync.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan@hemisync.ai>, procurement@hemisync.ai, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Hemisync demo — follow-ups & infra questions

Mateo / Dev — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Data residency: for PII lookup queries the customer agreement requires that tokens and raw request payloads stay in us-west. For non-PII queries we can allow failover to us-east. Can you make routing conditional on a "pii" flag in the request metadata?
2) Cost policy: we prefer a cost-aware default, but want an "override: latency" tag for specific flows (customer support). Can Redwood support per-route policy tags?
3) Reranker: can the reranker be invoked as an async job (we'd prefer to return search results fast, then enhance ranking for re-renders)?

Also — can you share the example fallback chain with expected cost deltas? We want to budget estimates before procurement. Procurement will also need an exportable mutual action plan and a short SLA excerpt.

Availability for the handoff call: 2028-03-15 16:00 PT or 2028-03-16 09:00 PT. Ethan will lead the technical side.

Sophia Cheng
Head of Platform | Hemisphere AI
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Cheng <sophia@hemisync.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Hemisync demo — follow-ups & infra questions

Thanks Sophia — answers inline and next steps.

1) Data residency by request flag: yes — we support request-scoped metadata and routing rules. We'll implement a request tag "pii=true" which pins route to us-west-only models. Example rule: match: request.metadata.pii==true -> enforce region: [us-west], deny failover.

2) Per-route policy tags: supported. You can mark a route with policy_tags: [latency_override] which forces latency-first routing even if cost thresholds are exceeded. We'll include this in the MAP.

3) Reranker async flow: supported. Typical pattern: return initial search results (top-20) quickly; kick async reranker job to produce an improved top-10 and send to client via webhook or store in DB for the UI to poll.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft with milestones and owners) and sdk_quickstart.yml. I've added an estimated cost delta table (high-level) in the MAP tab: llama-70b baseline ~ $X/1k tokens, 13b-8bit ~ ~0.3x, 7b-8bit ~ ~0.2x. We'll provide precise numbers in the procurement packet.

Next steps (action items):
- Confirm handoff: 2028-03-15 16:00 PT (Ethan) -> Mateo to send calendar invite.
- Redwood to provide final SLA excerpt and pricing export for procurement by 2028-03-17.
- Dev spike deliverables (SDK quickstart + auth checklist) shared (attached).
